newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold closes easier, seen trying lower levels.
newsitem.headline: HK gold closes easier, seen trying lower levels.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed easier on Friday after continued selling interest in Asia extended the decline that set in in New York overnight, and dealers said the yellow metal will further try the downside.
Bullion ended at US$347.70/348.20 an ounce, down from New York's US$348.50/349.00 close on Thursday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$349.00/50.

"Gold slipped in Asia today and New York overnight following the slump in the silver prices," said a dealer at a local investment house. Other bullion traders reported selling interest later as the U.S. dollar gained against the yen.
Dealers saw the market dropping further in coming days, but they said physical demand at around $345-346 levels should provide support.
Local gold ended HK$12 lower at HK$3,217 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to -4.00 from its previous fix at -5.00.
